sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Thinking in objects is like seeing the world as LEGO blocks - everything fits together! You'll learn how to design programs by modeling real-world things as objects.

• How to break problems into objects
• Why objects make code more organized
• How to design classes that work together

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine you're building a car. Instead of thinking about every single bolt and wire, you think about the big pieces: engine, wheels, seats. That's object-oriented thinking!

Objects are like those car parts - they bundle data (like size, color) with actions (like drive, brake).

• **Objects** = Things that exist (a specific car, a bank account)
• **Classes** = Blueprints for objects (the design of a car model)
• **Methods** = What objects can do (accelerate, withdraw money)

For example, a `Dog` class might have:
• Data: name, breed, age
• Actions: bark(), eat(), sleep()

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: Start design by identifying objects in the problem domain and their relationships
Each class should have a clear responsibility and represent a single concept
Define the data fields (attributes) each object needs to maintain its state
Define the methods (behaviors) that operate on the object's data
Use UML class diagrams to visualize class structure and relationships

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Objects = data + actions bundled together. Design starts with identifying real-world things. Practice by modeling everyday objects (phones, pets, etc.) Ready to learn about class relationships next.

questions.question: When modeling a real-world entity as a class, what should the data fields represent?
options: Properties or attributes of the entity
questions.explanation: Data fields should represent the properties or attributes of the real-world entity. For a Student class, fields might be name, age, and GPA.

questions.question: What should methods in a class represent when thinking in objects?
options: The behaviors or actions the entity can perform
questions.explanation: Methods represent the behaviors or actions that the entity can perform. For a BankAccount class, methods might be deposit(), withdraw(), and getBalance().
